subject: physics

moments.title: Doppler in Prague
moments.body: An Austrian physicist proposes that the colour of stars shifts depending on their motion towards or away from us. He uses this to (incorrectly) explain binary star colours. The colour idea is wrong; the principle is right.
moments.takeaway: A flawed application of a profound principle.

moments.title: Trumpeters on a train
moments.body: Dutch meteorologist Buys Ballot tests Doppler's theory by putting a group of trumpeters on an open railway carriage and listening to the pitch shift as they pass. The shift is audible and matches Doppler's prediction.
moments.takeaway: One of the most charming confirmations in physics history.

moments.title: Cosmological redshift
moments.body: Hubble's discovery that galaxies recede with speed proportional to distance is the Doppler effect applied to cosmology. Doppler's principle goes from acoustic curiosity to cosmological diagnostic.
moments.takeaway: Doppler's modest acoustic effect becomes the key to the universe's expansion.

moments.title: First exoplanet by Doppler
moments.body: Mayor and Queloz detect 51 Pegasi b — the first exoplanet around a Sun-like star — by measuring tiny Doppler wobbles of the star induced by its planet. They win the 2019 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Doppler's principle locates planets around other stars.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The Doppler effect is in police speed guns, weather radar, echocardiograms, GPS, and radio astronomy. Gravitational redshift, a relativistic cousin, is detected daily by GPS satellites.
now.open_questions: Can precision Doppler shifts detect Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zone of Sun-like stars?

reflection: Doppler's original explanation was wrong. Yet he gets the prize and the law. When should a wrong application of a right idea be credited?
